And Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tabarani informed us, in it, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qawhyar narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Hammad narrated to us. And Ahmad ibn Abi al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Nasr al-Sarakhsi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Aws narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Ju'dani, from Sulayman ibn Mirqa', from Hilal ibn al-Salt, that Abu Bakr said:

He said: "It benefits its companion with the good of this world and repels from him the terrors of the Hereafter, and it is called al-Dafi'a and al-Qadiya." [69] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/1.]]

And one who has tested it has related to me.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Ya-Sin: The reciters differed concerning it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf, in most transmissions, read "Yis" with a kasra on the ya', an intermediate pronunciation between the two sounds, the reading of the people of Madina, and this is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a kasra on the nun, likening it to "amsi," "raqash" and "hadhdham." Harun al-A'war read it with a damma on the nun, likening it to "mundhu," "haythu" and "qaṭṭ." Al-Sayyid al-Himyari said:

"O soul, do not cease to counsel sincerely, steadfast in affection, except for the family of Yasin..." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/4.]]

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "O chief of mankind."

﴿By the wise Qur'an. Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾ — this is the answer to the disbelievers' saying: "You are not a messenger."

﴿On a straight path.﴾ ﴿A revelation﴾: Ibn Amir and the people of Kufa read it with a fatha on the lam, as a verbal noun, as if he said "He revealed a revelation." It was also said: it is put in the accusative by way of departure from the description. The others read it with a damma, meaning: it is a revelation. ﴿The Mighty﴾: the Severe in restraint against the disbelievers; ﴿the Merciful﴾: toward His servants [[The manuscript has an unreadable word here; the reading given appears to be correct.]] and the people of His obedience.

﴿That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾: in the interval (fatra); it was also said: "with what their fathers were warned," so they are heedless of faith and right guidance.

﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and his companions of the Makhzum clan. That was because Abu Jahl had sworn that if he saw Muhammad praying he would crush his head. He came to him while he was praying, with a stone, to strike him; but when he raised it, his hand became stuck to his neck and the stone clung to his hand. When he returned to his companions and told them what he had seen, the stone fell off. A man of Banu Makhzum said: "I will kill him with this stone."

He came to him while he was praying to throw the stone at him, but Allah blinded his sight, so he began to hear his voice without seeing him. He returned to his companions, but did not see them until they called out to him and said: "What have you done?" He said: "I did not see him, but I heard his voice, and between me and him there was something like a stallion swishing its tail; had I come close to him, it would have eaten me." And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr al-Laythi narrated to us that al-Zuhri narrated to him, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz summoned Ghaylan al-Qadari and said: "O Ghaylan, it has reached me that you speak about predestination?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, they lie about me."

He said: "O Ghaylan, recite the beginning of Surat Ya-Sin." He recited: "Ya-Sin. I call you to witness, O Commander of the Faithful, that I repent of what I used to say about predestination." Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said:

"O Allah, if he is truthful, then accept his repentance; and if he is lying, then set over him one who will not show him mercy, and make him a sign for the believers."

He said: Hisham then seized him and cut off his hands and feet.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Abd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying:

My father narrated to us, from some of his companions, who said: Ibn Awn narrated this report from Muhammad ibn Umayr, and Ibn Awn said: "I saw him crucified at the gate of Damascus."

﴿You only warn those who follow the Reminder﴾: meaning, your warning benefits only those... — because he used to warn everyone — ﴿who follow the Reminder﴾: the Qur'an, acting upon it; ﴿and fear the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings﴾: inform him of ﴿forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We — it is We who bring the dead to life﴾ at the Resurrection; ﴿and We record what they have sent ahead﴾ of deeds, ﴿and their traces﴾: what was followed after them. Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba and al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning the Banu Udhra, whose dwellings were far from the mosque, so attending the prayers was hard for them; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces﴾, meaning their steps toward the mosque.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firabri narrated to us, saying: Hanan ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Harīrī, from Abu Nadra, from Jabir, from Abd Allah, who said: We wanted to move closer to the mosque, while the plots around the mosque were empty. The Prophet (ﷺ) heard of this and came to us in our homes and said: "O Banu Salama, it has reached me that you want to move closer to the mosque?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, the mosque is far from us, and the plots around the mosque are empty." He said: "O Banu Salama, stay in your homes, for your steps are being recorded." He said: So we did not wish, after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said what he said, to be in the vicinity of the mosque. [73] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 5/390.]]

Abu Ali al-Rudhbari informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Mahrawayh al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Qurra ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Utba ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, concerning His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces﴾, he said: "The steps on Friday."

﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear register﴾: We knew it, counted it and made it clear; ﴿in a clear register﴾ — this is the Preserved Tablet.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Baghawi narrated to us in Baghdad, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Shanbah al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Uthman ibn Salih al-Hannat narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Ali ibn Nudayma, who said: I heard Ikrima say: "Fa-a'shaynahum" with an unpointed ayn, and this was also narrated from Ibn Abbas.

﴿So they do not see.﴾ ﴿And it is alike to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah, saying: Umayr ibn Mirdas narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shabib narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Hanan ibn Zuhayr al-Adawi narrated to us, from his father, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr al-Laythi narrated to us that al-Zuhri narrated to him, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz summoned Ghaylan al-Qadari and said: "O Ghaylan, it has reached me that you speak about predestination?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, they lie about me."

He said: "O Ghaylan, recite the beginning of Surat Ya-Sin." He recited: "Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an..." up to His saying: ﴿And it is alike to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ Ghaylan said: "O Commander of the Faithful, by Allah, it is as if I had never recited it before today. I call you to witness, O Commander of the Faithful, that I repent of what I used to say about predestination." Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said:

"O Allah, if he is truthful, then accept his repentance; and if he is lying, then set over him one who will not show him mercy, and make him a sign for the believers."

He said: Hisham then seized him and cut off his hands and feet.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Abd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying:

My father narrated to us, from some of his companions, who said: Ibn Awn narrated this report from Muhammad ibn Umayr, and Ibn Awn said: "I saw him crucified at the gate of Damascus."

﴿You only warn those who follow the Reminder﴾: meaning, your warning benefits only those... — because he used to warn everyone — ﴿who follow the Reminder﴾: the Qur'an, acting upon it; ﴿and fear the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings﴾: inform him of ﴿forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We — it is We who bring the dead to life﴾ at the Resurrection; ﴿and We record what they have sent ahead﴾ of deeds, ﴿and their traces﴾: what was followed after them. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back﴾ [[Surat al-Qiyama: 13.]], and His saying: ﴿A soul will know what it has sent ahead and kept back﴾ [[Surat al-Infitar: 5.]].

Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba and al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning the Banu Udhra, whose dwellings were far from the mosque, so attending the prayers was hard for them; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces﴾, meaning their steps toward the mosque.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firabri narrated to us, saying: Hanan ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Harīrī, from Abu Nadra, from Jabir, from Abd Allah, who said: We wanted to move closer to the mosque, while the plots around the mosque were empty. The Prophet (ﷺ) heard of this and came to us in our homes and said: "O Banu Salama, it has reached me that you want to move closer to the mosque?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, the mosque is far from us, and the plots around the mosque are empty." He said: "O Banu Salama, stay in your homes, for your steps are being recorded." He said: So we did not wish, after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said what he said, to be in the vicinity of the mosque. [73] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 5/390.]]

Abu Ali al-Rudhbari informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Mahrawayh al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Qurra ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Utba ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, concerning His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces﴾, he said: "The steps on Friday."

﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear register﴾: We knew it, counted it and made it clear; ﴿in a clear register﴾ — this is the Preserved Tablet.

Makkan, and it has three thousand seven hundred and twenty-nine letters, eighty-three verses, and [the number of words is as stated in the text]. On its virtues:

Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Naqid informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed me, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Salih, from Harun Abu Muhammad, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Qatada, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin. Whoever recites Ya-Sin, Allah records for him, for reciting it, the reward of reciting the Qur'an ten times." [67] [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/456, with variation.]]

And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Multi in Egypt narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mahmud al-Nisaburi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Imran al-Razi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Umayr, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in the Qur'an there is a surah that intercedes for its reciter and forgives its listener. Verily, it is Surat Ya-Sin." [68] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/1.]]

And Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tabarani informed us, in it, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qawhyar narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Hammad narrated to us. And Ahmad ibn Abi al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Nasr al-Sarakhsi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Aws narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Ju'dani, from Sulayman ibn Mirqa', from Hilal ibn al-Salt, that Abu Bakr said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ya-Sin is called al-Mu'imma." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Mu'imma?" He said: "It benefits its companion with the good of this world and repels from him the terrors of the Hereafter, and it is called al-Dafi'a and al-Qadiya." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is that?"

He said: "It repels from him every evil and fulfils for him every need. Whoever recites it, twenty pilgrimages are credited to him; whoever hears it, he has a thousand dinars in the way of Allah; and whoever writes it and drinks it, a thousand remedies, a thousand certainties, a thousand nearnesses and a thousand mercies enter his [belly] [[In the manuscript: "jawfuha" (its belly).]], and every disease and shackle is removed from him." [69] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/1.]]

[71] [[Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/633, no. 8934.]]

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Hamza ibn al-Husayn ibn Umar al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Riyahi narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying:

Ayyub ibn Mudrik narrated to us, from Abu Ubayda, from al-Hasan, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever enters the graveyards and recites Surat Ya-Sin, the punishment is lightened for them that day, and he has as many good deeds as the number of those buried therein." [72] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/254.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Mahan narrated to us, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Amir ibn Yasaf al-Yamami narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Kathir, who said: It has reached us that whoever recites Ya-Sin in the morning will remain in joy until evening, and whoever recites it in the evening will remain in joy until morning. And one who has tested it has related to me.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Ya-Sin: The reciters differed concerning it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf, in most transmissions, read "Yis" with a kasra on the ya', an intermediate pronunciation between the two sounds, the reading of the people of Madina, and this is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

The rest read it with a fatha on the ya'. Abu Ja'far, Abu Amr, Hamza, Ayyub, Abu Hatim and Asim, in most transmissions, read "Yasin" with the nun clearly pronounced and quiescent.

It was also differed on from Nafi' and Ibn Kathir. Isa ibn Umar read "Yasa" with a fatha (on the final), likening it to "ayna" and "kayfa." Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a kasra on the nun, likening it to "amsi," "raqash" and "hadhdham." Harun al-A'war read it with a damma on the nun, likening it to "mundhu," "haythu" and "qaṭṭ." The others read it with the nun concealed (ikhfa').

The commentators differed in its interpretation. It was said: it is an oath. Ibn Abbas said: it means "O man" in the dialect of Tayy'. Ata said: it is in Syriac. Abu al-Aliya said: "O man." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "O Muhammad," the evidence being His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾.

Al-Sayyid al-Himyari said:

"O soul, do not cease to counsel sincerely, steadfast in affection, except for the family of Yasin..." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/4.]]

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "O chief of mankind."

If it is said: why was Ya-Sin counted as a verse while Ta-Sin was not counted as a verse?

The answer: Ta-Sin resembles "Qabil" in its pattern and its sound letters, whereas Ya-Sin begins with a letter of prolongation, and there is nothing like that in single nouns; so it resembled a sentence and a complete utterance, and it matched what follows of verse endings.

﴿By the wise Qur'an. Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾ — this is the answer to the disbelievers' saying: "You are not a messenger."

﴿On a straight path.﴾ ﴿A revelation﴾: Ibn Amir and the people of Kufa read it with a fatha on the lam, as a verbal noun, as if he said "He revealed a revelation." It was also said: it is put in the accusative by way of departure from the description. The others read it with a damma, meaning: it is a revelation. ﴿The Mighty﴾: the Severe in restraint against the disbelievers; ﴿the Merciful﴾: toward His servants [[The manuscript has an unreadable word here; the reading given appears to be correct.]] and the people of His obedience.

﴿That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾: in the interval (fatra); it was also said: "with what their fathers were warned," so they are heedless of faith and right guidance.

﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and his companions of the Makhzum clan. That was because Abu Jahl had sworn that if he saw Muhammad praying he would crush his head. He came to him while he was praying, with a stone, to strike him; but when he raised it, his hand became stuck to his neck and the stone clung to his hand. When he returned to his companions and told them what he had seen, the stone fell off. A man of Banu Makhzum said: "I will kill him with this stone."

He came to him while he was praying to throw the stone at him, but Allah blinded his sight, so he began to hear his voice without seeing him. He returned to his companions, but did not see them until they called out to him and said: "What have you done?" He said: "I did not see him, but I heard his voice, and between me and him there was something like a stallion swishing its tail; had I come close to him, it would have eaten me." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾.

﴿Around their necks are shackles, reaching to the chins, so they are held up.﴾ ﴿Muqmahun﴾: shackled. The root meaning of al-iqmah is lowering the gaze and raising the head. It is said: a camel is "muqmah" when it raises its head and lowers its gaze, and a camel is "qami'" when it has drunk water until it is sated, and so it "aqma'a." A poet, describing a ship he was in, said:

"And we sat along its sides, lowering our glances like camels that have been sated..." [[Al-Sihah: 1/397.]]

Abu Ubayda said: this is by way of a parable, and there were no shackles there; rather the meaning is: We hindered them from faith and from what they intended, with barriers, and so made the shackles a parable for that. In a report, Abu Dhu'ayb used to desire a woman in the pre-Islamic period; when he embraced Islam, the woman, whose name was Umm Malik, came to him and sought him for herself, but he refused and recited:

"There is no longer the old state of the abode, O Umm Malik, but the chains have encircled the necks..." [[Al-Sihah: 2/516.]]

"And the youth became like the old man, speaking nothing but justice, so the blamers have rested."  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/301.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Mahan narrated to us, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Amir ibn Yasaf al-Yamami narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Kathir, who said: It has reached us that whoever recites Ya-Sin in the morning will remain in joy until evening, and whoever recites it in the evening will remain in joy until morning. And one who has tested it has related to me.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Ya-Sin: The reciters differed concerning it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf, in most transmissions, read "Yis" with a kasra on the ya', an intermediate pronunciation between the two sounds, the reading of the people of Madina, and this is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a kasra on the nun, likening it to "amsi," "raqash" and "hadhdham." Harun al-A'war read it with a damma on the nun, likening it to "mundhu," "haythu" and "qaṭṭ." The commentators differed in its interpretation. It was said: it is an oath. Ibn Abbas said: it means "O man" in the dialect of Tayy'. Ata said: it is in Syriac. Abu al-Aliya said: "O man." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "O Muhammad," the evidence being His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾.

Al-Sayyid al-Himyari said:

"O soul, do not cease to counsel sincerely, steadfast in affection, except for the family of Yasin..." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/4.]]

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "O chief of mankind."

If it is said: why was Ya-Sin counted as a verse while Ta-Sin was not counted as a verse?

The answer: Ta-Sin resembles "Qabil" in its pattern and its sound letters, whereas Ya-Sin begins with a letter of prolongation, and there is nothing like that in single nouns; so it resembled a sentence and a complete utterance, and it matched what follows of verse endings.

﴿By the wise Qur'an. Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾ — this is the answer to the disbelievers' saying: "You are not a messenger."

﴿On a straight path.﴾ ﴿A revelation﴾: Ibn Amir and the people of Kufa read it with a fatha on the lam, as a verbal noun, as if he said "He revealed a revelation." It was also said: it is put in the accusative by way of departure from the description. ﴿That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾: in the interval (fatra); it was also said: "with what their fathers were warned," so they are heedless of faith and right guidance.

﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and his companions of the Makhzum clan. That was because Abu Jahl had sworn that if he saw Muhammad praying he would crush his head. He returned to his companions, but did not see them until they called out to him and said: "What have you done?" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾.

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr al-Laythi narrated to us that al-Zuhri narrated to him, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz summoned Ghaylan al-Qadari and said: "O Ghaylan, it has reached me that you speak about predestination?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, they lie about me."

He said: "O Ghaylan, recite the beginning of Surat Ya-Sin." He recited: "Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an..." up to His saying: ﴿And it is alike to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ Ghaylan said: "O Commander of the Faithful, by Allah, it is as if I had never recited it before today. I call you to witness, O Commander of the Faithful, that I repent of what I used to say about predestination." Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said:

"O Allah, if he is truthful, then accept his repentance; and if he is lying, then set over him one who will not show him mercy, and make him a sign for the believers."

He said: Hisham then seized him and cut off his hands and feet.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Abd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying:

My father narrated to us, from some of his companions, who said: Ibn Awn narrated this report from Muhammad ibn Umayr, and Ibn Awn said: "I saw him crucified at the gate of Damascus."

﴿You only warn those who follow the Reminder﴾: meaning, your warning benefits only those... — because he used to warn everyone — ﴿who follow the Reminder﴾: the Qur'an, acting upon it; ﴿and fear the Most Merciful unseen. Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba and al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning the Banu Udhra, whose dwellings were far from the mosque, so attending the prayers was hard for them; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces﴾, meaning their steps toward the mosque.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firabri narrated to us, saying: Hanan ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Harīrī, from Abu Nadra, from Jabir, from Abd Allah, who said: We wanted to move closer to the mosque, while the plots around the mosque were empty. ﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear register﴾: We knew it, counted it and made it clear; ﴿in a clear register﴾ — this is the Preserved Tablet.

Makkan, and it has three thousand seven hundred and twenty-nine letters, eighty-three verses, and [the number of words is as stated in the text]. On its virtues:

Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Naqid informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed me, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Salih, from Harun Abu Muhammad, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Qatada, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin. And Ahmad ibn Abi al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Nasr al-Sarakhsi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Aws narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Ju'dani, from Sulayman ibn Mirqa', from Hilal ibn al-Salt, that Abu Bakr said:

Al-Sayyid al-Himyari said:

"O soul, do not cease to counsel sincerely, steadfast in affection, except for the family of Yasin..." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/4.]]

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "O chief of mankind."

He said: "O Ghaylan, recite the beginning of Surat Ya-Sin." He recited: "Ya-Sin. Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Abd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying:

"And the youth became like the old man, speaking nothing but justice, so the blamers have rested."  [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/301.]]

The meaning is: We hindered them, by the barriers of Islam, from indulging in fornication and debauchery. Ikrima said: ﴿Indeed, We have placed around their necks shackles﴾ means darknesses and misguidances in which they were.

﴿And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see.﴾ ﴿Fa-aghshaynahum﴾: We made them blind. The common reading is with the ghayn (غ).

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed me, saying: al-Baghawi narrated to us in Baghdad, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Shanbah al-Baghdadi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Qasim Uthman ibn Salih al-Hannat narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Ali ibn Nudayma, who said: I heard Ikrima say: "Fa-a'shaynahum" with an unpointed ayn, and this was also narrated from Ibn Abbas.

﴿So they do not see.﴾ ﴿And it is alike to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah, saying: Umayr ibn Mirdas narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shabib narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Hanan ibn Zuhayr al-Adawi narrated to us, from his father, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr al-Laythi narrated to us that al-Zuhri narrated to him, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz summoned Ghaylan al-Qadari and said: "O Ghaylan, it has reached me that you speak about predestination?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, they lie about me."

He said: "O Ghaylan, recite the beginning of Surat Ya-Sin." He recited: "Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an..." up to His saying: ﴿And it is alike to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ Ghaylan said: "O Commander of the Faithful, by Allah, it is as if I had never recited it before today. I call you to witness, O Commander of the Faithful, that I repent of what I used to say about predestination." Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said:

"O Allah, if he is truthful, then accept his repentance; and if he is lying, then set over him one who will not show him mercy, and make him a sign for the believers."

He said: Hisham then seized him and cut off his hands and feet.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Abd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying:

My father narrated to us, from some of his companions, who said: Ibn Awn narrated this report from Muhammad ibn Umayr, and Ibn Awn said: "I saw him crucified at the gate of Damascus."

﴿You only warn those who follow the Reminder﴾: meaning, your warning benefits only those... — because he used to warn everyone — ﴿who follow the Reminder﴾: the Qur'an, acting upon it; ﴿and fear the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings﴾: inform him of ﴿forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We — it is We who bring the dead to life﴾ at the Resurrection; ﴿and We record what they have sent ahead﴾ of deeds, ﴿and their traces﴾: what was followed after them. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back﴾ [[Surat al-Qiyama: 13.]], and His saying: ﴿A soul will know what it has sent ahead and kept back﴾ [[Surat al-Infitar: 5.]].

Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba and al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning the Banu Udhra, whose dwellings were far from the mosque, so attending the prayers was hard for them; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces﴾, meaning their steps toward the mosque.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firabri narrated to us, saying: Hanan ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Harīrī, from Abu Nadra, from Jabir, from Abd Allah, who said: We wanted to move closer to the mosque, while the plots around the mosque were empty. The Prophet (ﷺ) heard of this and came to us in our homes and said: "O Banu Salama, it has reached me that you want to move closer to the mosque?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, the mosque is far from us, and the plots around the mosque are empty." He said: "O Banu Salama, stay in your homes, for your steps are being recorded." He said: So we did not wish, after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said what he said, to be in the vicinity of the mosque. [73] [[Sahih Ibn Hibban: 5/390.]]

Abu Ali al-Rudhbari informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Mahrawayh al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Qurra ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Utba ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, concerning His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces﴾, he said: "The steps on Friday."

﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear register﴾: We knew it, counted it and made it clear; ﴿in a clear register﴾ — this is the Preserved Tablet.

Makkan, and it has three thousand seven hundred and twenty-nine letters, eighty-three verses, and [the number of words is as stated in the text]. On its virtues:

Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Naqid informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed me, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Salih, from Harun Abu Muhammad, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Qatada, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin. Whoever recites Ya-Sin, Allah records for him, for reciting it, the reward of reciting the Qur'an ten times." [67] [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/456, with variation.]]

And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Multi in Egypt narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mahmud al-Nisaburi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Imran al-Razi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Umayr, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in the Qur'an there is a surah that intercedes for its reciter and forgives its listener. Verily, it is Surat Ya-Sin." [68] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/1.]]

And Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tabarani informed us, in it, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad ibn Qawhyar narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Hammad narrated to us. And Ahmad ibn Abi al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Nasr al-Sarakhsi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ayyub narrated to us, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Aws narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Ju'dani, from Sulayman ibn Mirqa', from Hilal ibn al-Salt, that Abu Bakr said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ya-Sin is called al-Mu'imma." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Mu'imma?" He said: "It benefits its companion with the good of this world and repels from him the terrors of the Hereafter, and it is called al-Dafi'a and al-Qadiya." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is that?"

He said: "It repels from him every evil and fulfils for him every need. Whoever recites it, twenty pilgrimages are credited to him; whoever hears it, he has a thousand dinars in the way of Allah; and whoever writes it and drinks it, a thousand remedies, a thousand certainties, a thousand nearnesses and a thousand mercies enter his [belly] [[In the manuscript: "jawfuha" (its belly).]], and every disease and shackle is removed from him." [69] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/1.]]

[71] [[Al-Jami' al-Saghir: 2/633, no. 8934.]]

Ayyub ibn Mudrik narrated to us, from Abu Ubayda, from al-Hasan, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever enters the graveyards and recites Surat Ya-Sin, the punishment is lightened for them that day, and he has as many good deeds as the number of those buried therein." [72] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/254.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Mahan narrated to us, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Amir ibn Yasaf al-Yamami narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Kathir, who said: It has reached us that whoever recites Ya-Sin in the morning will remain in joy until evening, and whoever recites it in the evening will remain in joy until morning. And one who has tested it has related to me.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Ya-Sin: The reciters differed concerning it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf, in most transmissions, read "Yis" with a kasra on the ya', an intermediate pronunciation between the two sounds, the reading of the people of Madina, and this is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

The rest read it with a fatha on the ya'. Abu Ja'far, Abu Amr, Hamza, Ayyub, Abu Hatim and Asim, in most transmissions, read "Yasin" with the nun clearly pronounced and quiescent.

It was also differed on from Nafi' and Ibn Kathir. Isa ibn Umar read "Yasa" with a fatha (on the final), likening it to "ayna" and "kayfa." Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a kasra on the nun, likening it to "amsi," "raqash" and "hadhdham." Harun al-A'war read it with a damma on the nun, likening it to "mundhu," "haythu" and "qaṭṭ." The others read it with the nun concealed (ikhfa').

The commentators differed in its interpretation. It was said: it is an oath. Ibn Abbas said: it means "O man" in the dialect of Tayy'. Ata said: it is in Syriac. Abu al-Aliya said: "O man." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "O Muhammad," the evidence being His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾.

Al-Sayyid al-Himyari said:

"O soul, do not cease to counsel sincerely, steadfast in affection, except for the family of Yasin..." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/4.]]

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "O chief of mankind."

If it is said: why was Ya-Sin counted as a verse while Ta-Sin was not counted as a verse?

The answer: Ta-Sin resembles "Qabil" in its pattern and its sound letters, whereas Ya-Sin begins with a letter of prolongation, and there is nothing like that in single nouns; so it resembled a sentence and a complete utterance, and it matched what follows of verse endings.

﴿By the wise Qur'an. Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾ — this is the answer to the disbelievers' saying: "You are not a messenger."

﴿On a straight path.﴾ ﴿A revelation﴾: Ibn Amir and the people of Kufa read it with a fatha on the lam, as a verbal noun, as if he said "He revealed a revelation." It was also said: it is put in the accusative by way of departure from the description. The others read it with a damma, meaning: it is a revelation. ﴿The Mighty﴾: the Severe in restraint against the disbelievers; ﴿the Merciful﴾: toward His servants [[The manuscript has an unreadable word here; the reading given appears to be correct.]] and the people of His obedience.

﴿That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾: in the interval (fatra); it was also said: "with what their fathers were warned," so they are heedless of faith and right guidance.

﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and his companions of the Makhzum clan. That was because Abu Jahl had sworn that if he saw Muhammad praying he would crush his head. He came to him while he was praying, with a stone, to strike him; but when he raised it, his hand became stuck to his neck and the stone clung to his hand. When he returned to his companions and told them what he had seen, the stone fell off. A man of Banu Makhzum said: "I will kill him with this stone."

He came to him while he was praying to throw the stone at him, but Allah blinded his sight, so he began to hear his voice without seeing him. He returned to his companions, but did not see them until they called out to him and said: "What have you done?" He said: "I did not see him, but I heard his voice, and between me and him there was something like a stallion swishing its tail; had I come close to him, it would have eaten me." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾.

﴿Around their necks are shackles, reaching to the chins, so they are held up.﴾ ﴿Muqmahun﴾: shackled. The root meaning of al-iqmah is lowering the gaze and raising the head. It is said: a camel is "muqmah" when it raises its head and lowers its gaze, and a camel is "qami'" when it has drunk water until it is sated, and so it "aqma'a." A poet, describing a ship he was in, said:

"And we sat along its sides, lowering our glances like camels that have been sated..." [[Al-Sihah: 1/397.]]

Abu Ubayda said: this is by way of a parable, and there were no shackles there; rather the meaning is: We hindered them from faith and from what they intended, with barriers, and so made the shackles a parable for that. [72] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/254.]]

And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Mahan narrated to us, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi, saying: Abd al-Rahman al-Muharibi narrated to us, saying: Amir ibn Yasaf al-Yamami narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Kathir, who said: It has reached us that whoever recites Ya-Sin in the morning will remain in joy until evening, and whoever recites it in the evening will remain in joy until morning. And one who has tested it has related to me.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Ya-Sin: The reciters differed concerning it. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf, in most transmissions, read "Yis" with a kasra on the ya', an intermediate pronunciation between the two sounds, the reading of the people of Madina, and this is the choice of Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim.

The rest read it with a fatha on the ya'. Abu Ja'far, Abu Amr, Hamza, Ayyub, Abu Hatim and Asim, in most transmissions, read "Yasin" with the nun clearly pronounced and quiescent.

Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a kasra on the nun, likening it to "amsi," "raqash" and "hadhdham." Harun al-A'war read it with a damma on the nun, likening it to "mundhu," "haythu" and "qaṭṭ." The commentators differed in its interpretation. It was said: it is an oath. Ibn Abbas said: it means "O man" in the dialect of Tayy'. Ata said: it is in Syriac. Abu al-Aliya said: "O man." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "O Muhammad," the evidence being His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾.

Al-Sayyid al-Himyari said:

"O soul, do not cease to counsel sincerely, steadfast in affection, except for the family of Yasin..." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/4.]]

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: "O chief of mankind."

If it is said: why was Ya-Sin counted as a verse while Ta-Sin was not counted as a verse?

﴿By the wise Qur'an. Indeed, you are among the messengers﴾ — this is the answer to the disbelievers' saying: "You are not a messenger."

﴿On a straight path.﴾ ﴿A revelation﴾: Ibn Amir and the people of Kufa read it with a fatha on the lam, as a verbal noun, as if he said "He revealed a revelation." It was also said: it is put in the accusative by way of departure from the description. ﴿That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless﴾: in the interval (fatra); it was also said: "with what their fathers were warned," so they are heedless of faith and right guidance.

﴿The word has certainly come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe.﴾ ﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and his companions of the Makhzum clan. That was because Abu Jahl had sworn that if he saw Muhammad praying he would crush his head. He came to him while he was praying, with a stone, to strike him; but when he raised it, his hand became stuck to his neck and the stone clung to his hand. When he returned to his companions and told them what he had seen, the stone fell off. A man of Banu Makhzum said: "I will kill him with this stone."

He returned to his companions, but did not see them until they called out to him and said: "What have you done?" He said: "I did not see him, but I heard his voice, and between me and him there was something like a stallion swishing its tail; had I come close to him, it would have eaten me." "There is no longer the old state of the abode, O Umm Malik, but the chains have encircled the necks..." [[Al-Sihah: 2/516.]]

﴿So they do not see.﴾ ﴿And it is alike to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah, saying: Umayr ibn Mirdas narrated to us, saying: Salama ibn Shabib narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Hanan ibn Zuhayr al-Adawi narrated to us, from his father, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. And Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Amr al-Laythi narrated to us that al-Zuhri narrated to him, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz summoned Ghaylan al-Qadari and said: "O Ghaylan, it has reached me that you speak about predestination?" He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, they lie about me."

He said: "O Ghaylan, recite the beginning of Surat Ya-Sin." He recited: "Ya-Sin. By the wise Qur'an..." up to His saying: ﴿And it is alike to them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ Ghaylan said: "O Commander of the Faithful, by Allah, it is as if I had never recited it before today. I call you to witness, O Commander of the Faithful, that I repent of what I used to say about predestination." Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said:

"O Allah, if he is truthful, then accept his repentance; and if he is lying, then set over him one who will not show him mercy, and make him a sign for the believers."

He said: Hisham then seized him and cut off his hands and feet.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, from al-Firabri, saying: Abd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying:

My father narrated to us, from some of his companions, who said: Ibn Awn narrated this report from Muhammad ibn Umayr, and Ibn Awn said: "I saw him crucified at the gate of Damascus."

﴿You only warn those who follow the Reminder﴾: meaning, your warning benefits only those... — because he used to warn everyone — ﴿who follow the Reminder﴾: the Qur'an, acting upon it; ﴿and fear the Most Merciful unseen. Al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba and al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning the Banu Udhra, whose dwellings were far from the mosque, so attending the prayers was hard for them; so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces﴾, meaning their steps toward the mosque.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Firabri narrated to us, saying: Hanan ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sa'id al-Harīrī, from Abu Nadra, from Jabir, from Abd Allah, who said: We wanted to move closer to the mosque, while the plots around the mosque were empty. Abu Ali al-Rudhbari informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Mahrawayh al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hatim al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Qurra ibn Habib narrated to us, saying: Utba ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, concerning His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And We record what they have sent ahead and their traces﴾, he said: "The steps on Friday."

﴿And everything We have enumerated in a clear register﴾: We knew it, counted it and made it clear; ﴿in a clear register﴾ — this is the Preserved Tablet.

Makkan, and it has three thousand seven hundred and twenty-nine letters, eighty-three verses, and [the number of words is as stated in the text]. On its virtues:

Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Naqid informed us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed me, saying: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Salih, from Harun Abu Muhammad, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Qatada, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur'an is Ya-Sin. Whoever recites Ya-Sin, Allah records for him, for reciting it, the reward of reciting the Qur'an ten times." [67] [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/456, with variation.]]

And Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Multi in Egypt narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Mahmud al-Nisaburi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Imran al-Razi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Umayr, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in the Qur'an there is a surah that intercedes for its reciter and forgives its listener. Verily, it is Surat Ya-Sin." [68] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/1.]]

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ya-Sin is called al-Mu'imma." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Mu'imma?" He said: "It benefits its companion with the good of this world and repels from him the terrors of the Hereafter, and it is called al-Dafi'a and al-Qadiya." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how is that?"

He said: "It repels from him every evil and fulfils for him every need. Whoever recites it, twenty pilgrimages are credited to him; whoever hears it, he has a thousand dinars in the way of Allah; and whoever writes it and drinks it, a thousand remedies, a thousand certainties, a thousand nearnesses and a thousand mercies enter his [belly] [[In the manuscript: "jawfuha" (its belly).]], and every disease and shackle is removed from him." [69] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 15/1.]]

[70] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 8/254, with variation.]]
